svg.title: Engine memory, cores and the copy ledger — 2026-10-20
svg.desc: An audit sheet, refreshed at HEAD f28262f0 on 2026-10-20: the path of one tick from the kernel to the strategy callback and every copy on it, the copy ledger, how the doctrine of 2026-09-19 stands against the code, what the alloc and copy gates prove, every thread and the core it asks for, the resident memory map, the cache-line layout, the CPU, clock and build facts, and each execution arm's own TX and RX ledger. Since the 2026-09-19 sheet the ring pop is a loan, so a tick costs two full-record copies (the capture stage and the ring publish), not three.
svg.text: Memory, cores and the copy ledger
a copy or gap no gate sees

text.tspan: what the engine actually does with RAM and CPU
· read from crates/ at HEAD f28262f0, 2026-10-20 — supersedes the 2026-09-19 sheet (bf088c0f) · companion to
docs/phase-8-architecture-v2.svg
and
docs/ai-strategy-pipeline.svg
Since 2026-09-19, ZC pass A made the ring pop a loan: a tick now costs TWO full-record copies, not three.
The capture stage is the copy no gate sees, and rustls' RX copies wait on rustls 0.24.

svg.text: also new on this sheet: 10 tick lanes and 128 B ring granules · 11 ingress crates, ten on one shared drain · the HL WebSocket gateway, Binance and Polymarket arms on the exec-gateway duplex · ≈ 21 threads at the current mask, not ~265 · ≈ 104.6 MiB attributable, not 53.6 · binary 11.2 MiB
THE PATH OF ONE TICK — every hop the bytes take, and what happens to them there

Ten hops from the wire to a strategy callback. Five move no bytes. Two are inside rustls. Of the three our code performs, the IoBuf fill is the doctrine's plaintext window, the ring publish is the designed copy, and the capture stage is the one no gate sees.
the read(2) copy every socket pays
plaintext lands in a Vec of its own — one
→ 4 MiB by venue; compacts only when
the tail pins full; one oversize guard for
a header and a payload RANGE; unmask
in place runs only if the frame is masked
a borrowed slice — no Vec, no
reassembly buffer; the raw tap copies
frame once and leave it untouched on
into a 64 KiB stage, before the push; no
// COPY: note, and core-io is outside
tail_cache is re-read only when the ring
the guard LENDS the slot; on_tick(&t)
reads it in place and Drop releases it —
= one gather + two copies (09-19: four). The old
top_k_into: the SoA ladder gathers its top 5 into the pair's spare row — 160 B
levels_equal, then commit flips DepthPair.last — an index, never a copy
192 B into the same 64 KiB stage, before the push
192 B into the depth lane's slot
one order, any member, paper or live
= two 64 B copies before the arm; each live arm then adds
its own (the exec ledger at the foot).
a 64 B Order handed over by value — a move, not counted
RoutedDispatcher::submit(&order): the risk gate and the ledger read it by
SlotCapture → the 64 KiB stage, in core-io again
the /state + TUI history keeps its own copy
HL /exchange · HL gateway · Binance · Polymarket — or the paper matcher

Depth lanes 2–3 carry the Polymarket rolling legs to the paper dispatcher only (one 160 B copy into the held book, core-fill held.rs:427); Hyperliquid's depth is captured and never rides a ring. Binance needs no symbol lookup (the sym is pinned to its socket); the others resolve through a boot-built, alloc-free SymbolMap (ingress-polymarket run_loop.rs:161).
THE COPY LEDGER — every copy of the payload bytes, counted
inside rustls — counted, not verified here
one allocation per record; gates 72 / 87c pin it
the one RX copy our own code performs
only when the tail pins full behind dead bytes
server frames are unmasked: no XOR in practice
a borrowed range; no reassembly buffer exists
Tick::new_stamped — a ≤ 64 B POD by value
BEFORE the push · core-io is outside copy-audit
a Popped guard lends the slot (09-19: a copy)
depth only; HL fills its row inside the parser
outbound; a refused order adds nothing
on the engine thread, AFTER the pop
no by-value temporary since ZC pass A
a pointer cast; the backtest then copies twice
Nothing on the ingest path touches the heap after boot except rustls' per-record Vec — every copy above lands in storage allocated once, at startup.
WHAT THE GATES PROVE — and what they cannot see
core_alloc::CountingAllocator wraps System and counts alloc / dealloc calls and bytes; AllocGuard asserts a zero delta around a region.
bench/tests/alloc_assertions.rs holds 140 #[test] fns — 136 run, 4 are #[ignore]d child helpers, gate numbers reach 136; docs/state.md's
"127/127" predates the PM15 / PMJ gates. --test-threads=1 and a fresh `Compiling bench` are required.
They measure HEAP ALLOCATION, not memcpy volume: five copy_from_slice calls into boot buffers report 0 B/op,
correctly. The suite cannot be cited for or against a copy count.
Bybit still has no alloc-gate coverage — ingress-bybit is not a bench dependency (MEXC, Hypercall and HyperEVM now are). No clippy lint
enforces any of this: clippy.toml has no disallowed-methods.
A RATCHET on the copy verbs (copy-audit.sh:102) against 27 baselined lines — signer-eip712 9 · ws_handshake 8 · transport 4 · ws_frame
3 · core-net lib 1 · boot_http 1 · json_encoder 1. Scope (:78-95): the exec lane and signers, core-net, core-ring, the ten market-data
ingress crates, the HYPARB / XMM / HCV / BIN15 / PM15 / PMJ members, core-fill, core-settle, engine, exec-gateway and the cli's live files.
NOT scanned: core-io (the capture copy), core-types, core-parse, book-builder, ingress-ai, strategy-vm, strategy-set. The
verb list cannot see a whole-struct assignment (= *x, = v): exec-polymarket's Out<Fill> push and pop pass unmarked
(arm.rs:269, 279) while the HL twin is marked (exec-hyperliquid arm.rs:684, 715).
One copy = one full-record memcpy of an already-formed record that our code performs. A ring transfer is now ONE: try_push_ref publishes into the
slot, try_pop_ref lends it back through a Popped guard and the callback reads it there.
DepthPair gather → capture stage → ring publish
capture + RecentRing — each live arm adds its own
file read → ring → VM ping-pong, at operator cadence
Under every one of them, per TLS record: rustls 0.23 copies twice and allocates once before our IoBuf copy — open by operator ruling until rustls 0.24
THE DOCTRINE NOW — the 2026-09-19 ruling against the code
the operator ruling, as CLAUDE.md prints it:
“Everything that CAN be done zero-copy IS … PODs are copied once into their ring slot (Producer::try_push_ref) and read there in place
(Consumer::try_pop_ref lends the slot through a Popped guard).”
what the code does at f28262f0:
the pop is a loan on every ring — no try_push / try_pop is left in the tree
every ingress parser fills the caller's frame in place (&mut Frame → bool)
the top-K change gate flips a DepthPair; the last-snapshot copy is gone
the ten market-data drains share core_net::drain and one oversize guard
capture is a second full-record copy per tick, taken BEFORE the push, in core-io — no // COPY: note, and copy-audit does not scan
rustls: two internal copies and one allocation per record on every socket, until 0.24
So a tick costs two, not one. Both copies are designed; only the ring publish is marked. On 2026-09-19 the count was three —
the pop copy is what ZC pass A removed.
THREADS AND CORES — what the process actually schedules
run_engine_loop: eng.tick(256), the 16-slot set inline, the /state seqlock publish; the HL /exchange arm's sockets when that arm boots
INGRESS — one thread per venue, each its own single-writer producer
PM CLOB WSS — the daily tokens
EVERY Binance market socket on one mio poll: spot + 2 × (usdm + dated + coinm + coinm_dated) + 1 eapi
the AI command plane: UDS, HMAC, seq, the ruleset validator
OKX v5 public WSS + L2 book walk
Deribit JSON-RPC WSS + L2 book walk
HL public WSS; a cold /info re-read between sessions
MEXC spot protobuf + futures JSON; N = ⌈spot/15⌉ + ⌈perp/13⌉; a client heartbeat
HyperEVM pool events → the pool Signal ring
Hypercall WSS; REST /options-summary handed over an SPSC
min(8, families) market sockets + 1 RTDS socket; Gamma REST discovery
SERVICES AND WRITERS — off the loop, never pinned
the ratatui dashboard over the same snapshot cell
the HAR long-tenor state, written off the loop (H3.7)
EXEC ARMS — only when their slot is live
the HL WS order gateway: 2 make-before-break sockets + a REST fallback; a 30 s client heartbeat
every Binance exec socket (≤ 5 lanes × 2 WS-API sessions + user + risk stream + REST); the journal; the resolver
slot 9's CLOB REST + the redeemer; the Polymarket user WS
the core map describes intent; on the M4 none of it binds

pin_current_thread_to_core() calls sched_setaffinity(2) on Linux (cli/src/pinning.rs:59-86); everywhere else pin_impl returns Err(Unsupported) (:92-95) and the thread floats — one WARN per pinned ingress thread (paper.rs:11187-11203), INFO for the gateways. main is never pinned.
Two requests collide, on Linux only: bn-gateway asks for core 10, as ingress-hyperevm does (bn_live.rs:87); hl-gw-* ask for 12, as ingress-pm15 does (xmm_live.rs:130).

No thread sets .stack_size(): every one takes std's 2 MiB default. At the mask docs/state.md records (2815, ten members) with one HL gateway arm up, ≈ 20–22 threads reserve ≈ 42 MiB of VIRTUAL stack plus main's — the 09-19 sheet's ~265 threads / ~530 MiB was wrong even then: Binance has run every socket on ONE thread since M1c (bad65d63, 2026-08-22).
RESIDENT MEMORY — where the bytes live, allocated once at boot and never resized

≈ 104.6 MiB attributable at the universe docs/state.md records — 254 Binance sockets, 7 + 7 Polymarket rolling market sockets, one HL gateway arm; the Binance arm (≈ 12.3 MiB of buffers) is not booted
network RX / TX + held HTTP buffers
INLINE ON THE ENGINE THREAD'S STACK

text.tspan: rings:

38 in Rings::new (cli/src/paper.rs:619-722) + three hand-offs = ≈ 16.87 MiB. head and tail are each a Padded in a 128 B granule and buf starts at offset 256; the OrderEvent ring is never instantiated in production.
capture staging, counted this time:

11 PmlrCapture (pm, pm15, pm5, bn, okx, deribit, hl, bybit, mexc, hypercall, hyperevm) × 5 writers (ticks, events, signals, opt-summary, depths) × 64 KiB, + 3 engine SlotCaptures (fills, orders, events) + 2 raw taps (RAW_TAP=pm,hl) = 3.75 MiB (core-io capture.rs:146-205; paper.rs:3265-3281).
every member is built at boot, whatever the mask:
member_table! expands to Self { $f: <$ty>::new() } (strategy-set/src/lib.rs:293-297), so an unarmed slot still pays its box; the HAR, xmm and hcv blocks are the configure-time exceptions.
allocated ≠ resident:

IoBufs and stages are vec![0u8; N] (calloc) and the big blocks alloc_zeroed — macOS commits a page on first touch; the hyparb tick maps are the exception (vec![EMPTY; n] writes every byte). Each Binance socket costs 68 KiB: 12 sockets instead of 254 take the total to ≈ 86.6 MiB.
not in the total:

thread stacks (≈ 21 × 2 MiB, virtual) · the binary, 11.20 MiB on disk (09-19: 5.22) · rustls' internals for ≈ 285 TLS sessions · per-connection Driver structs. Production runs the platform allocator: #[global_allocator] exists only in two test binaries (bench alloc_assertions.rs:23, signer-ed25519 tests/drop_wipes.rs:53).

svg.text: CACHE-LINE LAYOUT — the hot types, and the padding that keeps writers apart
every ring-carried POD is #[repr(C, align(64))] + Copy and size-asserted at compile time; the DepthPair that feeds the depth lanes is the one hot carrier without an assert
core-types lib.rs:2326 — one `last` byte forces line 7
HlCmd · ExecEvent · BnCmd · BnEvt · PmCmd · PmEvt · JupIntent · JupEvent
64 B each, const-asserted in duplex() with NE ≥ 4 · NC

text.tspan: RuleTableV2 = 256 rows × 128 B + one metadata line = 32 832 B · 513 lines
— still deliberately NOT AsBytes: the validator builds it in memory and nothing parses it from wire bytes. AsBytes has 10 impls; there is no FromBytes, no bytemuck, no zerocopy crate. Tick v3
carries venue_time_ms at offset 56 and its STALE flag in flags (core-types lib.rs:358-414). UserFill (88 B) is a plain repr(C) scratch row, never ring-carried.

svg.text: padding that exists to stop false sharing, not to round a number

text.tspan: core_ring::Padded

head and tail each alone in a 128 B granule, repr(C, align(128)) — the M4 reports hw.cachelinesize 128 and x86 prefetches 64 B lines in pairs (core-ring lib.rs:130-138, asserted :728-729); buf starts at offset 256. The cached indices live in the private handles —
Producer {head, tail_cache}, Consumer {tail, head_cache}, three words each (:262-272, :364-373, :685-686).
engine_snapshot::SnapshotCell

still a single-writer seqlock with seq alone on a 64 B line ahead of the payload (cell.rs:38-40) — a Mutex was refused because Darwin's pthread mutex heap-allocates on first lock. On the M4's 128 B line, seq now shares a granule with the
payload's first 64 B.
core_metrics::Counter / Gauge
align 64, 128 B each — name[64], then value at offset 72 (registry.rs:155-156).
new 128 B granules

SharedNonce — one CAS per agent address (exec-hyperliquid nonce.rs:81-87); AnchorSlot and TopupSlot; GatewayStats, 83 456 B of single-writer granules: engine-written, engine-rare, the halt word alone, gateway-written, gateway-live, published
(exec-gateway stats.rs:185-220).
core_ring::Mailbox
a one-slot cold hand-off for the HAR and HCV snapshots — no padding, by design (mailbox.rs:75-83).

svg.text: #[repr(C, align(64))]: 132 attributes in 76 files (09-19: “34 files”) · align(128): 12 attributes in 5 files — the cross-thread structures are now laid out for the M4's 128 B line.
clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW) — NTP slew cannot move it (core-time lib.rs:49-70). ts_ns orders; venue time is data: Tick v3's venue_time_ms
+ STALE flag, and FeedClock judges each connection's offset and staleness in nine run loops plus OKX's (core-time ~:140-240). WallAnchor pairs the
clocks once at boot. The raw tap takes its own clock read (binance run_loop.rs:760, 776).
LatencyTracker records with THREE relaxed fetch_adds — bucket, sum_ns, count — and finds a percentile by cumulative scan (core-latency :104-147).
The bucket array is always 32 × 64 AtomicU64 = 16 KiB whatever ROWS is; <24> uses 1 536. The engine keeps 3 × <24>; each gateway arm adds 5
one scalar byte_sum() and two tests, and no crate depends on it. No std::arch, NEON or AVX kernel exists, and no prefetch. The vector work is
memchr's: memmem::find at 182 call sites and memchr at 53, across 16 crates. One SWAR site: exec-binance cid.rs:162-204.
ring push and pop: a masked get_unchecked(pos & (N − 1)) (core-ring :252) and one cache-miss branch each — the Rigtorp refresh. 29 non-test
get_unchecked in the tree; documented branch-free code in exec-router (route.rs:467, 490; ledger.rs:1514's search), exec-hyperliquid cloid.rs:97,
THE EXEC LANE'S COPY LEDGER — one order out and one fill in, per arm (replaces the E7 addendum of 09-19)
Every arm renders into its final buffer and pays the doctrine's two transport copies out; what differs is how many 64 B PODs move between threads. Every row below lands in boot-allocated storage.

The legacy sign_order budget gate (≤ 1 alloc, ≤ 256 B, alloc_assertions.rs:1074) sits over a OnceLock'd context (signer-eip712 lib.rs:78-81): 09-19's ‘~208 B per signature’ is one boot allocation; the order path is 0 B (gates

text.tspan: exec-router

no copy of the Order: RoutedDispatcher, the risk gate and the ledger read it by reference and derive a 24 B RestingOrder from its fields (routed.rs:1161-1197, ledger.rs:613-646); fills are booked by reference (routed.rs:1648).
Hypercall · HyperEVM · Jupiter

Hypercall orders are operator verbs only (hypercall-live): the body is rendered in place and EIP-712-signed over its own spans (gates 83, 84). HyperEVM rides hyparb-live, chain 998 by config: EIP-1559 → [u8; 65], the raw-tx hex rendered into the HttpsPost body (gates 64, 66, 71). A live slot 11 refuses the boot, so Jupiter's arm is never built (exec_boot.rs:115-126; gates 134, 135).
0 B/op on the order path

HL encode + sign 54 · envelope → scan 58 · requote 60 · gateway engine half 96a · gateway outcome mode 103 · Binance signers 104 · PM order path 115, 130 · Jupiter 134 · EVM 64 · Hypercall 83. rustls' residue, pinned exactly: 2 allocations per post or request (72, 77b, 87b, 101, 114). Loopbacks: hl_userws, hl_gateway, hl_exchange_tls, bn_e2e.

svg.text: STALE COMMENTS AND SMALL DEFECTS — found by reading the code, worth fixing at the source

text.tspan: engine/src/lib.rs:72

“five rings = 5 MiB” — NUM_TICK_LANES is 10 (:102), so 10 MiB; :13 still says five tick lanes and four fill lanes (10 and 5), :15 “two atomic loads” (one Acquire load with the cached head). Flagged 09-19 at :64 — still there, and further off.
the T1–T7 topology table and “cores 0..=7”: requests now run 1–13 and core 0 is never asked for; the loop comment says main pins core 0 — main is never pinned.
cli/src/xmm_live.rs:128-129
“the next past the ingress threads' 1–11”: pm15 and pm5 took 12 and 13, so hl-gw-* now share 12 with ingress-pm15, and bn-gateway shares 10 with ingress-hyperevm.
core-io/src/lib.rs:6-15
“pwrite-based append”, “Phase 0 ships the shape”: the writer is write_all on an O_APPEND file, and it carries the capture copy.
exec-router/src/routed.rs:166
“the ledger (146 048 B …)”: ledger.rs:872 asserts 161 408 since the PM15 re-pins.
bench/tests/alloc_assertions.rs

gate 114 is numbered twice (:17672 the HL gateway's REST path, :20320 the PM15 ingress driver); gate 72's doc (:10955) says the unbuffered API removes the residue — the rustls plan §1.3 refutes that (a TL7 item).
core-types/src/lib.rs:2326
DepthPair — 448 B, 7 lines, the one hot carrier without a size assert; its single `last` byte costs a whole line.
signer-eip712 · exec-polymarket
sign_order's doc still says “~208 B per call”; PmArm's Out<Fill> copies (arm.rs:269, 279) carry no // COPY: note while the HL twin's do.
fixed since 09-19
engine/src/lib.rs's RuleTable slot comment now says “~32 KiB” (:993), and core-types asserts 32 KiB + 64 (:6463).

svg.text: Every verdict was established by reading the code at f28262f0, not the comments; file:line is given for each (crates/ is implied). Counts that depend on
the deploy — sockets, which arms are up, har.toml's series — take docs/state.md's record of 2026-10-19; /state on 127.0.0.1:9191 is the truth, and
nothing on this sheet is live state.
the honest sentence, for whoever writes the next doctrine line:
“Counting every full-record memcpy our code performs: a tick costs two — the PMLR capture stage and the ring publish, the pop being a
loan; a depth event one gather and two; an order two before its arm; an inbound fill three on the HL /exchange arm and up to eight 64 B
moves on the gateway arms; a RuleTable three, at operator cadence. Every copy lands in boot-preallocated storage; after startup only
rustls touches the heap — one Vec per record and two allocations per post — until rustls 0.24.”
